pageContent: An old article has been found printed on a poster from back in 1851, kindly uploaded by our readers, the text is as follows:

1st of July 1851 - The Silver Mine at Black Pine was officially declared 'Exhausted' today after no further seams have been discovered for over two months of digging.  Work is set to dismantle the extraction machinery and rails, and move along to dig out a new extraction shaft, where more seams of Silver Ore were discovered during prospecting.

images.caption: The last day of the Silver Mine at Black Pine, 30 June 1851

pageContent: John Baxley was one of the most distinguished photographers that gave up hours of his time to help our club.  Originally a Police Diver and Photographer, he was famous in his working life for working and surveying the scene for some of the most high profile cases of his time, including but not limited to the infamous unsolved Arnie Spencer Tragedy, as it came to be known.  He joined our club in 1928 following his retirement from the North West Mounties.  Here we can see John in a rare photo with the Mounties Search Party in August 1901 before starting work in the Old Silver Mine at Black Pine, he is normally on the other side of the lens!

images.alt: John Baxley and the Mounties search party outside Black Pine Silver Mine Shaft B, August 1901

Margaret McLeod lived a quiet and practical life in rural Ontario following her husband's retirement from the North West Mounted Police. The couple settled near Maple Grove, where Margaret became closely involved in the running of their small property.

She maintained a modest apple orchard and, during the autumn months, sold apples, preserves and other produce directly to families in the surrounding communities. The orchard was never a large commercial operation, but it became a familiar local source of fresh fruit and a modest supplement to the household income.

Margaret and William remained together on the property for the rest of their lives. She continued tending the orchard and garden after William's death in 1943, maintaining the simple rural life they had built together away from his former career on the frontier.
